steps.title: Apply display: grid to the container
steps.instruction: Add the CSS property `display: grid;` to the container element to enable grid layout.
steps.hint: Look for the CSS rule that targets the container class or element, then add the display property inside it.

steps.expectedOutcome: The container element will become a grid container, allowing you to use grid properties to arrange its child elements.
successCriteria: The CSS rule for the container includes `display: grid;`.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully turned the container into a grid container. This is the foundation for creating a grid layout.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added `display: grid;` to the container's CSS rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container is not yet a grid container. Add `display: grid;` to the container's CSS rule.

steps.title: Set up grid-template-columns with fixed width
steps.instruction: Inside the .container rule, add the property grid-template-columns with the value repeat(3, 200px) to create three fixed-width columns.
steps.hint: Use the grid-template-columns property to define column sizes. The repeat() function creates multiple columns with the same width.
steps.seedCode:
<!-- Create your HTML structure here -->

/* Add your CSS rules here */
.container {
  display: grid;
  /* Add grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 200px); here */
}
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container rule will have grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 200px) creating three 200px wide columns.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added fixed-width columns to the grid container.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 200px) inside the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid-template-columns property with repeat(3, 200px) is missing from the .container rule.

steps.title: Add grid gap for spacing
steps.instruction: Add a gap property to the .container selector to create spacing between the grid cards.
steps.hint: Use the CSS property 'gap' with a value like '20px' to add consistent spacing between grid items.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container selector now includes a gap property, which will create visual spacing between the grid cards when the CSS is applied.
successCriteria: The .container selector includes a gap property with a valid CSS length value (e.g., 20px).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added spacing between the grid cards using the gap property.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the gap property is correctly added to the .container selector with a valid value like '20px'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The gap property is missing or incorrect. Check that you've added 'gap: [value];' inside the .container selector.

steps.title: Introduce the repeat() function with auto-fit
steps.instruction: In the .container rule, change the grid-template-columns value from repeat(3, 200px) to use repeat(auto-fit, 200px).
steps.hint: Replace the existing grid-template-columns value with repeat(auto-fit, 200px) to make the grid responsive.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid will now automatically create as many 200px columns as can fit in the container width.
successCriteria: The .container rule has grid-template-columns set to repeat(auto-fit, 200px).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've updated the grid to use auto-fit, which will make it responsive to different container widths.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've replaced the entire grid-template-columns value with repeat(auto-fit, 200px).
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid-template-columns value should be repeat(auto-fit, 200px). Check that you've replaced the previous value correctly.

steps.title: Combine auto-fit with minmax() for flexible columns
steps.instruction: Update the grid-template-columns property in the .container rule to use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)) instead of the fixed repeat(3, 200px).
steps.hint: Replace the existing grid-template-columns value with repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)). This creates columns that are at least 200px wide but can grow to fill available space.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container rule should have grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)); creating flexible responsive columns.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully updated the grid to use auto-fit with minmax(). This creates columns that automatically adjust to fit the container while maintaining a minimum width.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've replaced the entire grid-template-columns value with repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)). Check for any typos or missing parentheses.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid-template-columns property should be updated to use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)). This combines auto-fit with minmax() to create flexible responsive columns.

steps.title: Add container padding and center alignment
steps.instruction: Add padding to the .container rule and use margin: 0 auto to center it horizontally on the page.
steps.hint: Add padding and margin properties inside the existing .container selector.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will have internal spacing and be centered horizontally on the page.
successCriteria: The .container rule includes padding and margin: 0 auto properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added padding and centered the container, improving the overall layout.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to add both padding and margin: 0 auto to the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding padding and margin: 0 auto properties to the .container selector.

steps.title: Enhance card content styling
steps.instruction: Add font styling and internal spacing to the card content for better readability. Set the font-family to 'Arial, sans-serif', line-height to 1.6, and add 20px of padding inside each card.
steps.hint: Use the font-family, line-height, and padding properties on the .card selector.
steps.expectedOutcome: The card content will have improved typography and spacing, making it more readable.
successCriteria: The .card selector includes font-family: 'Arial, sans-serif', line-height: 1.6, and padding: 20px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've enhanced the card content with better typography and spacing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include all three properties: font-family, line-height, and padding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The card styling isn't complete. Check that you've added font-family, line-height, and padding properties to the .card selector.

steps.title: Test responsiveness by resizing the viewport
steps.instruction: Resize your browser window to observe how the grid automatically adjusts the number of columns based on available space.
steps.hint: Drag the edge of your browser window to make it narrower or wider, and watch how the cards rearrange themselves.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will see the grid columns automatically adjust as you resize the browser window, demonstrating the power of auto-fit with minmax().
successCriteria: The grid responds to viewport changes by adjusting the number of columns without any media queries.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully observed how auto-fit creates a fully responsive grid that adapts to any screen size.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Try resizing the window more dramatically to see the full effect of auto-fit.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid doesn't seem to be responding. Make sure your grid-template-columns uses repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...)) and that you're actually resizing the browser window.
